accuracy.evidence: Each mechanism behaves as the real object does: a torch push-switch toggles on and off with each press, a tap handle opened further gives a bigger flow, a wind-up toy stores energy in a coiled spring so more key turns give a longer run (the lab caps it at 4 turns, as real toys have a stop), a zip slider joins the teeth as the tab is pulled, and a clothes peg is a lever with a spring so squeezing the ends opens the jaws. The curriculum line 'Explore how things work' was checked against Development Matters (2023) for 3- and 4-year-olds.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets animism and magical thinking documented by Piaget and in early-years science guidance ('the toy wants to walk', 'it is magic', 'it stopped because it is tired'), plus action slips seen with toddlers: shaking or blowing on a torch, turning a tap the wrong way for more water, pulling the coat instead of the zip tab and pulling a peg's mouth open instead of squeezing the ends.

lab_distinct.evidence: Five object-specific mechanisms built for this topic: a torch push-switch with a beam, a tap handle that rotates through four flow levels and fills a cup in real time, a wind-up toy whose run length is set by the number of key turns and leaves labelled markers, a zip slider dragged up a coat, and a press-and-hold peg that opens while held and clamps a sock on release. The shingle gate passed against every other flag lab and none of these interactions appears in 310 Pushes and Pulls or 375 Wondering and asking why.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child causes every effect before the text names it: the torch task needs on then off, the tap task needs a full cup and then the tap turned back to off, the toy task needs two runs with different winds so the longer run is seen beside the shorter one, and the peg task needs three squeeze-and-release cycles. Each finish line states the cause-and-effect rule, e.g. 'Turn more: more water. Turn back: it stops.'

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions with tempting wrong options: what the torch button does ('Make the torch bigger'), what turning the tap more does ('Less water comes out' listed first), how far three winds go ('Just the same') and what squeezing a peg does ('It shuts tight', the intuitive answer since squeezing usually closes things). The lab then shows each result and the reveal names the prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven questions with fourteen tagged slips, each answered with the part that really does the job, e.g. 'A toy is not alive. It cannot want things. You wound up its spring, and the spring makes it walk.', 'Waiting will not wind it. The spring has run down, so turn the key again.' and 'Pulling the coat does not join it. Pull the little tab.' In-lab wrong actions (pressing the handle, letting go with no winds, letting go of a shut peg, pulling the coat) also get their own message.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use one- and two-syllable words (press, turn, key, spring, tap) in sentences of about six words and pass the family FK limit of 5.0; 'spring' is introduced with what it does. Canvas headings are four words or fewer ('Tap: lots', 'Socks on the line: 2 of 3'). The adult text uses the precise early-years terms: cause and effect, Understanding the World, mechanism words press, twist, squeeze and wind.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler scan and the 12% explanation-overlap gate against all 515 lessons. Each kid paragraph adds a new mechanism or the try-and-watch method, the adult text adds the curriculum line, safe objects, words to model and the named mistakes, and nothing restates the key idea.

mobile.evidence: Checked screenshots after Show me on every step at Android 360 px dark and iPhone 13 light. Controls are full-size lbtn buttons in pairs ('Turn it more' / 'Turn it back', 'Squeeze the peg' / 'Let go'), the canvas parts can also be tapped or dragged directly, the wind-up toy was enlarged after the first screenshots and its run markers moved below the track so labels no longer overlap, and the zip progress label moved under the coat.

accessibility.evidence: The browser gate ran axe WCAG 2.1 AA on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations and no console errors. Every drag or tap on the canvas has a button twin with an aria-label (Press the torch button, Turn the tap more, Turn the key on the toy, Pull the zip tab up, Squeeze the ends of the peg), and the canvas aria-label follows each spoken message.
